newsitem.title: USA: Dow surges to record, large caps extend dominance.
newsitem.headline: Dow surges to record, large caps extend dominance.

text.p: The Dow industrials stormed higher on Tuesday, tallying their 13th record close this year, with large-cap stocks extending their run as the favored class on Wall Street.
The Dow gained 78.5 points to close unofficially at an all-time high of 7067.46. The large-cap rally also pushed the S&P 500 and NYSE Composite indices into record territory.
Analysts said several factors played into the rally, including the strength of the U.S. dollar, and, somewhat ironically, a heightened sense of caution about the market.
"People are cautious," said Peter Coolidge, senior equity trader at Brean Murray and Co. "People are buying quality, people are buying more liquid names."
Keeping with a recent trend, the session was fairly uneventful until the final moments, when a wave of program buying propelled the Dow higher.
The demand for stocks did not broaden out to technology or smaller-cap names, however. The Russell 2000 small-cap index eked out a nominal gain and the tech-laden Nasdaq Composite finished lower.

"With the dollar acting as well as it has, foreign investors have stepped up their buying," said Alan Ackerman, market strategist at Fahnestock & Co. "They tend to focus on the large-cap stocks because they're more liquid."

Leading the Dow's advance was Philip Morris Cos Inc, which jumped 5-7/8 to 131-3/8 amid speculation that tobacco companies were working together toward a broad settlement of lawsuits against the industry.
Other tobacco companies also posted sharp gains. RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp rose 1-7/8 to 37-3/8, and UST Inc gained one to 31-3/4.
Other Dow components rising on the day were Procter & Gamble Co, up 4-3/8 to 129-1/4, and Boeing Co, up 2-1/4 to 110.

Elsewhere, the session was marked by a flurry of merger news led by H.F. Ahmanson and Co's surprise $6.0 billion stock offer to buy Great Western Financial Corp . Great Western shares surged 10-3/4 to 45.

"The Ahmanson premium represents three times book value so maybe we're at a new high in terms of what one is willing to pay for these thrifts," said Richard Cripps, chief market strategist at Legg Mason Wood Walker.
"But these deals are very much stock driven, so yes we're in a high market but if your currency is stock, perhaps the price is not as much as it would appear," Cripps added.
H.F. Ahmanson shares also jumped after news of the offer, closing at 44-7/8, up 4-3/8 on the day.

Other deals announced Tuesday included Marriott International Inc's agreement to acquire Renaissance Hotel Group NV for $1.0 billion cash, or $30 per share. The agreement nullified an $890 million deal that Renaissance had previously reached with Doubletree Corp.
Shares in Marriott gained one to 56-1/4, and Renaissance shares rose 4-5/8 to 29-3/4. Shares in Doubletree climbed 2-1/2 to 43-1/8.
Horizon/CMS Healthcare Corp rose 2-1/4 to 16-1/2 after the company agreed to a stock-swap acquisition by HealthSouth Corp. HealthSouth shares fell 2-1/8 to 41.

Shares in Evergreen Media Corp fell 1-1/4 to 31-1/2 after the company announced it would acquire Chancellor Broadcasting Co in an all-stock deal. The companies also said they planned to acquire 10 radio properties from Viacom Inc for $1.075 billion after completing their merger.
Shares in Chancellor rose 1/16 to 28 and Viacom shares gained 1-5/8 to 35.
The Nasdaq Composite fell 1.40 points to 1365.79.
The S&P 500 index rose 7.81 points to 816.29.
The Russell 2000 rose 0.92 of a point to 370.05.
((-- Wall Street desk, 212-859-1730))
